title: Playing bass and banjo at a birthday party
summary: The interviewer recalls Sing playing bass in a tux and banjo with a tall bassist; Sing says he plays piano, bass and banjo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Chester had to go in and park the car. Because I remember one party, remember that, it was your niece's birthday, remember? And sing came, and who was that old bass player there, was it a real old one, a famous old bass player, was there?
At my niece's birthday.
Yeah, don't you remember at your niece's birthday party?
Well, thank you.

Well no, maybe it was your birthday, it was one of your birthday parties, that's what it was. It was your birthday party about four years ago, and it was an old bass player, I forget what his name was, and a couple of people asked him to play, and I don't know who had been playing the bass, and then sing said, oh, and he didn't want to play, and sing said I'm going to play. And I said I didn't know you could play the bass thing. And sing said, sure, I can play the bass and I can play the banjo too. But then after sing played, then he got up and played a number. I'm trying to think of who, he was real old, and he hasn't played in years and years and years. I can't. It wasn't Darcy, were you?
No, it wasn't Darcy.

This was somebody who, but he wouldn't play until sing, sing got up and played a little bit on the bass, and then he came up and he said, come here, I'm going to show you how to do it, young fella. And then sing went over and took the banjo, and played the banjo. And I didn't have the camera that day.
Connor Brownson?
Yeah, a tall, very tall fella. Tall, slim.
Yeah, that's Tarnas' brother, Fouché.
Fouché, yeah, that was his name, Fouché. He played bass.
Yeah, he played trumpet, he played trumpet. No, Tarnas played trumpet, but this is his brother, he played bass and guitar. Yeah, yeah.

Yeah, and you remember that now? Yeah. But he wouldn't play until Sing got up and played, yeah, Fouché. Yeah, I remember, I knew if I heard his name. But I was glad I was there that night, because every time when we show the pictures, you know.
Well, see if I'd continue playing a bass, I'd be a nice bass player.
Well, I think we'd do fine right now.
You know, I mean, I think I'd be a better bass player than I am, and I would have no more positions, you know. I would have no more positions. And then my hand got tipped to the bass, you see. Yeah.

But every time we show those pictures, you know, when all these foreign kids come in, they come over and see the pictures, and when that one flashes, they say, Look at Sing at the bass, and what's he got a tux on for? He got all dressed up, and he got all, you know, everybody else in the band sitting in shirt sleeves, and you were in your tux. But the first thing they say is, Look at Sing on the bass. And then we tell them the story about how you got there late. What else do you play? Banjo, bass, piano? That's all.
That's all.
And sing?
That's all.
